questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

There is no doubt that Oltmans is (1)/ a very good coach and helped an (2)/ Indian cricket team take bold strides. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: The error lies in part 2 of the sentence as the article 'an' is incorrect and must be replaced with 'the' as the Indian cricket team is something specific.'An' is used to refer to one object. It should read as:'a very good coach and helped the..'

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

The rival teams scored three goals (1)/ with 10 circle penetrations against us and (2)/ we did scored just one off 15.(3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option (3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error in part (3) is with the verb form "did scored." When using "did" for emphasis or to form a past tense question or negative, the main verb should be in its base form, making the correct construction "did score" rather than "did scored."
 
• The phrase "off 15" is correctly written as "o

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Only one of the students ______ not done the homework given yesterday.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Has'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The verb here should be singular as the subject is singular, which is 'one of the students.'
 
• It refers to one student only. Moreover the verb 'done' hints us that the verb here should be in present perfect tense.
 
• Thus 'has' fits here correctly. Option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Government is trying to _________ the former glory of Red Fort.
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

 
• **Create**=> generate; produce
 
• **Rehab**=> a course of treatment for drug or alcohol dependence, typically at a residential facility, a building that has been rehabilitated
 
• **Restore**=> to bring back the former state of something
 
• **Survive**=> persist

 

Thus, **option 3** ie. **restore **makes proper sense here to convey that the Government is trying to bring back the previous glory of the Red Fort.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

A safe and secure

P: women to take up a variety

Q: environment may allow more

R: of jobs or run a business
questions.solution: Q is the first part of the sentence as it answers a safe and secure what. P follows Q to state allow more whom. R completes the sentence by mentioning a variety of what. Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question:

Q: after few years of use

R: which will get exhausted
questions.solution: P is the first part of the sentence as the word 'resources' fits correctly after the word 'non-renewable.' Q does not make any sense after P but R gives a proper definition that what these are. Thus option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: A person with ______ morals is involved in good
questions.solution: The sentence talks about a person involved in good deeds thus the morals should be good as well. Option 2 is the correct answer. The word 'neutral' means 'not taking any side' and 'transient' means 'short-lived.'

questions.question: It right in ______ to the society
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Sedating=> calm (someone) or make them sleep by administering a sedative drug

Irritating=> annoying

Adapting=> make (something) suitable for a new use or purpose

Adopting=> choose to take up or follow (an idea, method, or course of action)

Thus option 3 is the correct word here conveying the meaning that some people consider it to be necessary to adjust to the society they live in.

questions.question: Actually having bad ______
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Murals=> a large picture that has been painted on the wall of a room or building

Corals=> a hard stony substance secreted by certain marine coelenterates

Cultural=> relating to the ideas, customs, and social behaviour of a society.

Morals=> principles

Thus option 4 is the correct word conveying the meaning that people who think bad deeds are correct to live in today's society have bad morals or principles.

questions.question: Wrong deed or even a ______ crime
questions.solution: The word 'even' mentions the extremity of the situation thus the word 'serious' which means 'grave' fits perfectly before the word 'crime.' It means that a person with bad morals will not feel bad to commit even a serious crime. The other words do not convey any meaning here. 'Casual' means 'relaxed and unconcerned' and 'mere' means 'only.' Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Person is ______ up that decide his actions
questions.solution: The word here should fit with the preposition 'up'. Thus 'brought up' which means 'raised' is the correct answer here. Option 4 means that a person's morals is decided by his/her way of growing up or the way he/she is raised. The other words do not convey any meaning here. 'Sort' means 'arrange.'
